## Overview

Complete kv-C from #49569 and enable MyPy for `tests/v1/kv_connector`, following the [approved claim](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/49569#issuecomment-6312150429). PR 9's parent/root scope in #62891 is unchanged.

## Claims

- All 108 connector Python files pass MyPy 1.20.2 targeting Python 3.11 and 3.12.
- Route the directory through `SILENT_GROUPS`, preserving parent and other routing.
- Restore the previously uncollected MLA notification test using the current handshake contract and a local config, with no Hub download.

## Validation

Rebased onto `b1f5f61559`. Validated commit: `146b56ceaa`.

- Complete directory MyPy for both targets, the actual all-files MyPy hook, applicable pre-commit on the full PR diff, and commit hooks pass.
- CPU selection: **1234 passed, three skipped**. Untouched pinned main: **1233 passed, the same three skips**. JUnit comparison finds no missing case or changed common outcome; the additional pass is the restored MLA test.
- Store worker/scheduler/HMA and NIXL compressed-layout cases: **386 passed, five existing layout skips**.
- NIXL Push, descriptor geometry and the MLA test: **366 passed**.
- MyPy with `--platform darwin`: the old affinity guard produces one `sched_setaffinity` error; the Linux guard passes.
- MLA with an empty HF cache, no HF credentials, offline flags and a Python outbound-connection guard: **one passed**, with zero connection attempts and no HF cache files created. The old fixture fails constructing the remote model config in an empty offline cache.
- Temporary wrong-ID controls fail at the original broadcast and READ payload assertions. No deliberate defect is retained.

These selections overlap. Local GPU/NCCL, physical NIXL/RDMA and ROCm/MORI validation remains unavailable: driver 550.144.03 cannot initialize the installed PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130 build, and ROCm/MORI dependencies are absent. The results above are local; hosted CI results for this revision are not yet available. Actual optional NIXL/GPU job selection still needs checking.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

Pytest and lint use separate environments; substitute their paths for `.venv` below. The same CPU selection was run on untouched pinned main.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m mypy --python-version 3.11 --follow-imports silent --warn-unused-ignores tests/v1/kv_connector
.venv/bin/python -m mypy --python-version 3.12 --follow-imports silent --warn-unused-ignores tests/v1/kv_connector
pre-commit run mypy --all-files --hook-stage manual
pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --files $(git diff upstream/main...HEAD --name-only)
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit -m cpu_test -q -rs --timeout=90 -W error::pytest.PytestUnraisableExceptionWarning
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py::test_mla_broadcast_notif_uses_remote_request_id -q --timeout=90
```

</details>

## Details

The MLA test was nested inside `test_handshake_decode_errors`, so pytest never collected it. Its registration call and READ assertions had drifted. The restored test runs the real asynchronous handshake: decode TP=1 reads from prefill rank 0 and notifies ranks 1–3. Both the READ completion and broadcasts must carry the remote prefill request ID, rather than the local decode ID. Only external transport is faked.

Its config is now a real one-layer `DeepseekV2Config` saved under `tmp_path`, retaining the MLA dimensions used by the fixture. With no HF cache or credentials, the test still passes. Replacing either notification ID in memory makes it fail with `decode-req-AAAA:1` versus required `prefill-req-BBBB:1`. This restores coverage; it does not claim a production request-ID defect. The active `v1-others-cpu` command selects it; collection with that working-directory and marker convention confirms one case.

The review cleanup removes 88 redundant scheduler hash wrappers, keeps 13 required by typed `ReqMeta` boundaries, and adds `_hashes()` for repeated worker lists. Scheduler `BoundaryPut` construction now matches upstream. The three specified lifetime-sensitive method overrides use `type: ignore[method-assign]`, and monkeypatch parameters are regular arguments. Original assertions, decorators and async cleanup are preserved. No production change, relaxed assertion, retry or new skip is included.

I checked the issue and related work before opening this PR; #62891 covers the separate parent/root rollup. AI assistance was used for implementation and local checks.
